headline: Approved four sets of previous meeting minutes and reviewed library safety data and event permitting barriers
summary: The committee adopted four sets of previous meeting minutes as a group. Library staff presented data on trespass incidents showing declines after adding an embedded outreach worker and in-house security. The committee also discussed barriers to public space programming and event permitting with input from BCA, Parks, and DPW staff, but took no formal action on that topic.
decisions: Adopted four sets of previous meeting minutes as a group.

PARKS, ARTS & CULTURE COMMITTEE 
Meeting Minutes – August 11, 2026 (Draft) 
Meeting conducted in person and via Zoom 
Call to Order 
The meeting was called to order at 12:09 PM by Chair Councilor Allie Schachter.  
Technical difficulties occurred at the start of the meeting regarding room audio and Zoom 
connections; these were resolved before proceeding.  
Attendance 
Committee Members: 
• Chair Councilor Allie Schachter 
• Councilor Carter Neubieser (Zoom) 
• Councilor Becca Brown McKnight (Zoom) [PACC Trans...pt 8.11.26 | Word] 
City Staff & Presenters: 
• Mary Danko (Fletcher Free Library) 
• Jeff Nicholson (City Data Analyst) 
• Phil Lewis (BPRW) 
• Doreen Kraft (BCA) 
• Jackie Esperiti (DPW) 
• (name?) BFD 
• Jessica Brown (CA), via Zoom 
• Hayley McClenahan (CA) 
• Jennifer Zakaras 
• Samantha McGinnis (CSMP) 
Members of the Public: 
• Chris McGrath   
Approval of Previous Minutes 
Chair Schachter noted that four sets of meeting minutes were sent in advance and posted on Civic 
Clerk. She requested a motion to adopt them as a group. 
• Motion: Councilor Neubieser
• Second: Councilor McKnight 
• Approved unanimously 
Public Forum 
• One attendee, Chris McGrath, introduced himself and shared no specific concerns. 
• No additional public comments in person or online. 
 
Presentation – Fletcher Free Library Hotspot Strategy 
& Safety Staffing Update 
Presenters: 
• Mary Danko, Library Director 
• Jeff Nicholson, City Data Analyst 
Overview 
Mary Danko introduced two major strategic changes implemented at the library to address 
increasing challenging behaviors: 
1. Embedding a Howard Center Street Outreach Team member at the library. 
2. Transitioning from contracted security to in-house security staff. 
These changes were implemented with mayoral support.   
Library Trespass Ordinance & Data Background 
Mary provided context regarding the Library’s specific ordinance, established pre-COVID, defining 
the library as a limited public forum and detailing rules for behavior and graduated trespass levels 
(Classes A–D). 
Mary and Jeff Nicholson presented data showing monthly trespasses, types of trespasses, staff 
time spent, and behavior-related incidents, noting significant decreases following implementation 
of outreach + in-house security staffing.  
Key Data Trends 
• Clear decline in total trespasses after outreach specialist and security guard started. 
• Reduced frequency of severe incidents (Class A). 
• Staff time spent per trespass decreased. 
• Howard Street Outreach specialist able to intervene before situations escalate. 
• Library staff report noticeable improvements in workplace experience.   
• Summer 2024 saw a peak of 60+ incidents in a rolling 30-day window.
• Security currently covers 7 days/week. 
• Howard Center outreach position covers Tuesday–Saturday. 
Mary hopes to expand outreach coverage to 7 days/week.  She is seeking grants and has mayoral 
support.  
Discussion – Barriers to Public Space Programming & 
Event Permitting 
Chair Schachter introduced a conversation stemming from June budget discussions. 
Purpose: Identify barriers for outside groups who wish to program public spaces, with goal of 
expanding activation across Burlington while balancing staff capacity and budget constraints. 
Recent launch of OpenGov event portal noted as a developing tool.  
Committee Member Perspectives 
Councilor McKnight 
Raised two key questions: 
1. How can Burlington increase outside-group programming so the city provides space but 
external partners take on staffing and production? 
2. How can the city ensure proper permitting and enforcement, especially for informal or 
pop-up events?  
Councilor Neubieser 
Asked for clarity on: 
• Economic goals of expanding events (revenue vs. cost vs. saturation). 
• ROI of city-sponsored activation. 
• How Burlington’s level of support compares with other municipalities. 
• Budget implications of increasing or shifting city involvement.  
City Staff Contributions 
BCA (Doreen) Comments 
• Staff capacity is extremely strained; large festivals require major administrative workload. 
• Some fee restructuring at Waterfront Park successfully increased bookings. 
• Need clearer priority setting from Council to focus staff strategy. 
• Suggested shared Google Doc for cross-department barrier identification.  
Parks (Phil Lewis)
• Waterfront Park bookings strong; weekends nearly full. 
• Impact fees for events were recently adjusted based on producer feedback. 
• Battery Park remains challenging due to safety environment and staffing limitations.   
DPW (Jackie) 
Outlined DPW involvement: 
• Parking signage and meter bagging (requires 24-hour notice). 
• Street closures require coordination with BPD and DPW Streets Division. 
• Large events (e.g., marathon) require trucks, barricades, water department involvement. 
• Scale of event determines necessary permitting (e.g., tent inspection by Fire Marshal)
